docs.title: RMS Check
docs.text: RMS Check is a linter for AoE2:DE's flavour of RMS. This website hosts the documentation for all the cool maths going into the checker

docs.title: 1. Notation
docs.text:
• \(G\) is a proposition, the current Guard.
  • \(L\) is a set of name/guard pairs \((n, g)\) meaning \(n\) is live when \(g\) is true
  • \(L[n] = ot\) if \(n otin L\)
  • \(L_1 \sqcup L_2 = \{(n, L_1[n] \lor L_2[n])\ orall\ n \in L_1 \cup L_2\}\) (read as \(L_1\) joined with \(L_2\))
  • At a use-site:
    • \(n\) is definitely-live if \(G \implies g\) for some \((n, g) \in L\)
    • \(n\) is definitely-dead if \(G \implies eg g\) for some \((n, g) \in L\)
    • \(n\) is maybe-live if \(G \implies g\) or \(G \implies eg g\) cannot be derived.
  • Probability:
    • \(P_{k,n}(x)\) is the guard of block \(k\) arm \(n\). It can be derived if \(x \geq 100\).
    • \(P_{k,n}(0) = ot\) and \(P_{k,n}(100) = op\).
    • \(P_{k,1}(x_1) \lor ... \lor P_{k,n}(x_n) = P_{k,1..n}(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i)\)
    • Lemma 1: \(P_{k,n}(x_1) \land P_{k,m}(x_2) = ot\)
    • Lemma 2: \(P_{k,n}(x_1) \land eg P_{k,m}(x_2) = P_{k,n}(x_1)\)
    • Lemma 3: \( eg P_{k,n}(x_1) \lor eg P_{k,m}(x_2) = op\)
    • Lemma 4: \((P_{k,1}(x_1) \land g) \lor (P_{k,2}(x_2) \land g) = g\) iff \(x_1 + x_2 \geq 100\)
  • \(L, G \vdash ar{S} \implies L'\) set \(L\) is updated to \(L'\) when analysing statements \( ar{S}\) along with the current guard \(G\) (read as \(L, G\) yield \( ar{S}\) implies \(L'\)).
  • \[ egin{array}{rc} { t (rmsLaCase)} & egin{array}{c} egin{array}{cc} C_1 & C_2 \end{array} \ \hline S_1 \end{array} \end{array} \]

is read as \(C_1 \land C_2 \implies S_1\)

docs.title: 2.1. Sequence
docs.text: \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaSeq)} & \begin{array}{c}         \begin{array}{ccc}             L, G \vdash S \implies L'             & L', G \vdash \bar{S} \implies L''         \end{array}         \\ \hline         L, G \vdash S \bar{S} \implies L''     \end{array} \end{array} \]

docs.title: 2.2. Include DRS
docs.text: \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaIncDrs)} & \begin{array}{c}         \begin{array}{ccc}             {\tt PATH} \vdash \bar{S}             & L, G \vdash \bar{S} \implies L'         \end{array}         \\ \hline         L, G \vdash {\tt \#include\_drs\ PATH} \implies L'     \end{array} \end{array} \]

docs.title: 2.3. Include XS
docs.text:
\[ \begin{array}{rc} {\tt (rmsLaIncXs)} & \begin{array}{c} \begin{array}{ccc} {\tt PATH} \vdash \bar{S} \end{array} \\ \hline L, G \vdash {\tt \#includeXS\ PATH} \implies L \end{array} \end{array} \]

Note: including XS files has no effect on the RMS file's namespace

docs.title: 2.4. Const/Label Definitions
docs.text: \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaConstDef)} & \begin{array}{c}         L, G \vdash {\tt \#const\ NAME\ VALUE} \implies L \sqcup \{({\tt NAME}, G)\}     \end{array} \end{array} \] \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaLabelDef)} & \begin{array}{c}         L, G \vdash {\tt \#define\ NAME} \implies L \sqcup \{({\tt NAME}, G)\}     \end{array} \end{array} \]

docs.title: 2.5. If-Else
docs.text:
\[ egin{array}{rc} { t (rmsLaIfElse)} & egin{array}{c} egin{array}{c} L, G \land C_1 \vdash S_1 \implies L_1 \ \color{yellow} L, G \land eg C_1 \land ... \land eg C_{i-1} \land C_i \vdash S_i \implies L_i \ \color{orange} L, G \land eg C_1 \land ... \land eg C_n \vdash S_e \implies L_e \end{array} \ \hline L, G \vdash { t if}\ C_1\ ar{S_1}\ {\color{yellow}{ t elseif}\ C_2\ ar{S_2}\ ... \ { t elseif}\ C_n\ ar{S_n}}\ {\color{orange}{ t else}\ ar{S_e}} \implies L\ \sqcup igsqcup_i\ L_i \end{array} \end{array} \]

Note: the elseif and else branches in an if are optional, and may be skipped. In that case, \(S_i = \epsilon\)

docs.title: 2.5. Random
docs.text: \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaRandom)} & \begin{array}{c}         \begin{array}{c}             L, G \land P(p_i) \vdash S_i \implies L_i\         \end{array}         \\ \hline         L, G \vdash {\tt start\_random}\ {\tt percent\_chance\ p_1}\ \bar{S_1}\ ...\ {\tt percent\_chance\ p_n}\ \bar{S_n}\ {\tt end\_random} \implies L\ \sqcup \bigsqcup_i\ L_i \end{array} \end{array} \]

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
start_random
    percent_chance 50 #define A
    percent_chance 50 #define A
end_random

From the two arms of this block:

  • \(L_1 = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50))\}\)
  • \(L_2 = \{(A, P_{1,2}(50))\}\)

Which join into \(L = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50) \lor P_{1,2}(50))\} = \{(A, \top)\}\)

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
start_random
    percent_chance 50 #define A
    percent_chance 50 #define B
end_random

start_random
    percent_chance 50
        if A
            #define NAME1
            #define NAME2
        endif
    percent_chance 50
        if A
            #define NAME1
        endif
        if B
            #define NAME2
        endif
end_random

From the two arms of the first block:

  • \(L_1 = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50))\}\)
  • \(L_2 = \{(B, P_{1,2}(50))\}\)

Which join into \(L = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50)), (B, P_{1,2}(50))\}\)

Then from the arms of the subsequent block:

  • \(L_1 = \{({\tt NAME1}, P_{2,1}(50) \land A), ({\tt NAME2}, P_{2,1}(50) \land A)\}\)
  • \(L_2 = \{({\tt NAME1}, P_{2,2}(50) \land A), ({\tt NAME2}, P_{2,2}(50) \land B)\}\)

which finally join to produce

\[L = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50)), (B, P_{1,2}(50)), ({\tt NAME1}, (P_{2,1}(50) \land A) \lor (P_{2,2}(50) \land A)), ({\tt NAME2}, (P_{2,1}(50) \land A) \lor (P_{2,2}(50) \land B))\}\]

which simplifies to \(L = \{(A, P_{1,1}(50)), (B, P_{1,2}(50)), ({\tt NAME1}, A), ({\tt NAME2}, (P_{2,1}(50) \land A) \lor (P_{2,2}(50) \land B))\}\)

docs.title: 2.8. Block
docs.text: \[ \begin{array}{rc}     {\tt (rmsLaBlock)} & \begin{array}{c}         \begin{array}{ccc}         L, G \vdash \bar{S} \implies L'         \end{array}         \\ \hline         L, G \vdash \{\ \bar{S}\ \} \implies L'     \end{array} \end{array} \]
